Measured 2026-09-16 on patstat_2026_spring through /v1/patstat/query: the verified entry ep_oppositions_by_year returned patstat_sql_timeout cold and succeeded on an immediate retry, and portfolio_by_year_office took 20.0 s cold against 1.8 s warm — same SQL, same edition, nothing changed but the cache. RE-MEASURED 2026-09-17 AFTER A DELIBERATE DATABASE RESTART, AND THAT CLIFF IS GONE: all 34 verified entries ran cold without a single timeout, the slowest at 5.1 s, ep_oppositions_by_year at 4.5 s and portfolio_by_year_office at 4.5 s — the visibility-map VACUUM, the narrowing of three entries and the pinned planner statistics each contributed. Every verified entry now records BOTH numbers, as runtime_ms.cold and runtime_ms.warm in verified-queries.yaml, cold being wall time through this route on that sweep; the header of that file says exactly what was and was not measured. THE RETRY IS STILL THE RIGHT FIRST MOVE — these tables are still far larger than the cache and the mechanism has not changed — but treat a cold timeout as the exception now rather than the expected first call, and when you quote an entry's runtime to a user, say WHICH of the two numbers you are quoting. SO, ON A TIMEOUT: resubmit the SAME SQL once, with retryOf, BEFORE changing anything. If the second call also times out, that is a real cost signal rather than a cold cache — narrow the question then (a year floor, a tighter applicant or CPC anchor, an aggregate instead of a row listing) and never send the identical SQL a third time. FIRST CHECK WHICH CHANNEL YOU ARE ON, because on one of them the resend has already happened: the FlowLeap CLI resends ANY 5xx automatically, twice, 250 ms and 500 ms apart (client.rs send_retrying, FLOWLEAP_MAX_RETRIES, silent unless you pass -v), so a 504 that reaches you through `flowleap patstat query` is the THIRD identical failure and the retry is spent — narrow it, do not send it again. A slow SUCCESS on that channel is the same mechanism showing its other face: a 34 s wall time on a 20 s statement timeout is a cold attempt that failed and a warm one that worked, not a query that ran for 34 s. Over raw HTTP (/v1/patstat/query direct) nothing retries for you and the one identical resend is yours to make. THE OTHER SQL ERRORS ARE THE OPPOSITE, so do not treat this as a general retry licence: patstat_sql_forbidden (403), patstat_sql_too_expensive (422), patstat_sql_invalid (400) and patstat_sql_error (400) each say the SQL itself must change, and an unchanged resubmission fails identically while spending the 10-per-minute budget. THREE OF THE 503s ARE NOT ABOUT YOUR SQL AT ALL, and they are different from each other. patstat_busy (503) is LOAD: every guarded-SQL slot is taken, so keep the SQL exactly as it is and wait out the Retry-After delay. patstat_unreachable (503) is an OUTAGE: the PATSTAT database, the tunnel to it or the connection pooler is down or restarting, NOTHING is wrong with your SQL, and rewriting it cannot help — honour Retry-After and resend the SAME query, and if it is still failing after a couple of rounds say so plainly rather than inventing a narrower question. patstat_unavailable (503) is PERMANENT for this deployment: PATSTAT was never configured here, so no retry will ever work and you should answer from the document layer (the EPO/USPTO tools) or tell the user the analytics surface is not available. input.question: Which CPC codes do 'perovskite tandem cell' filings actually use?
input.sql:
SELECT c.cpc_code, s.title, COUNT(DISTINCT a.family_id) AS families, COUNT(DISTINCT a.application_id) AS applications
FROM flowleap.application_texts t
JOIN flowleap.applications a ON a.application_id = t.application_id
JOIN flowleap.classifications c ON c.application_id = t.application_id
LEFT JOIN flowleap.cpc_scheme s ON s.symbol = c.cpc_code
WHERE UPPER(t.title) LIKE '%PEROVSKITE%' AND UPPER(t.title) LIKE '%TANDEM%'
GROUP BY c.cpc_code, s.title
ORDER BY families DESC
LIMIT 40

**Perovskite tandem filings cluster in H10K (organic/hybrid devices), with the silicon bottom cell pulling in H10F and the Y02E tags added on top.** Two sources agree: a Google Patents corpus slice of about 130 publications whose abstracts say "perovskite tandem", and a PATSTAT 2026 Spring query on applications whose title contains both "perovskite" and "tandem".

Subclass level, from the Google Patents slice, counted as classification entries:

| Subclass | Entries | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| H10K | 1027 | Organic and hybrid electric solid-state devices |
| H10F | 226 | Inorganic semiconductor devices sensitive to radiation (the former H01L31) |
| Y02E | 106 | Climate-mitigation tag for energy generation |
| H01L | 49 | Legacy pre-2023 classification |
| H01G | 48 | Capacitor-type photoelectrochemical cells |

Subgroup level, from PATSTAT, counted as DOCDB families:

| CPC code | Families | Scheme title |
|---|---|---|
| Y02E10/549 | 59 | Organic PV cells |
| H10K85/50 | 47 | Organic and hybrid organic-inorganic perovskites, e.g. CH3NH3PbI3 |
| H10K30/57 | 46 | Comprising multiple junctions, e.g. tandem PV cells |
| H10K30/40 | 30 | p-i-n structure, e.g. perovskite absorber between charge transport layers |
| H10K39/15 | 24 | Comprising both organic PV cells and inorganic PV cells |
| H10F10/19 | 19 | Multiple potential barriers of different types, e.g. tandem with PN and PIN |
| H10K30/10 | 19 | Heterojunctions between organic and inorganic semiconductors |
| H10K30/50 | 16 | Photovoltaic devices |
| Y02P70/50 | 15 | Manufacturing processes characterised by the product |
| H10F10/161 | 12 | Multiple PN heterojunctions, e.g. tandem cells |
| H10K71/12 | 12 | Liquid deposition, e.g. spin coating |
| H10K30/82 | 11 | Transparent electrodes, e.g. ITO |

Practical takeaways for building a search:

- **Core trio for the concept.** H10K85/50 identifies the perovskite material, H10K30/57 identifies the tandem architecture, and H10K39/15 catches organic-on-inorganic stacks like perovskite on silicon. Combining the first two with AND is the tightest anchor.
- **Silicon bottom cells live in H10F.** H10F10/19, H10F10/161, H10F10/166 for silicon heterojunction cells, and H10F19/40 for mechanically stacked four-terminal devices. Perovskite-on-silicon filings routinely carry both an H10K and an H10F code.
- **Y02E10/549 is the most common single code** but it is a tag applied to all organic PV, so it is a poor discriminator on its own.
- **Older filings carry H01L31 and H01G9/20 codes.** H01G9/2072 explicitly covers tandem photoelectrodes. Include the legacy codes if your search reaches back before the 2023 to 2025 reclassification into H10K and H10F.
- **Process claims** show up under H10K71 subgroups for deposition and annealing, and under H10F71 for the inorganic side.

The PATSTAT counts are limited to title matches, so they understate the total but reflect the code mix reliably. Recent years are incomplete because of the 18-month publication lag.
